_comment: Dual GitHub account routing. Read by scripts/github/gh-for.ps1,
apply-commit-identity.ps1 and verify-github-accounts.ps1.
AUTH AND COMMIT IDENTITY ARE SEPARATE QUESTIONS. Conflating them was the
first design's mistake.
AUTH follows the repo's REMOTE OWNER, and there is no choice about it. A
repo whose remote is Rev4nchist/fourth-salesforce-mcp MUST authenticate as
Rev4nchist -- that is who owns it; the company account would simply 404.
So auth is derived, not configured: see authByOwner.
COMMIT IDENTITY is a policy choice, and Dave's is: Fourth work is authored
as david.hayes@fourth.com even when the repo happens to live in the
personal namespace. Attribution should reflect whose work it is.
WHY AN EXPLICIT REPO LIST AND NOT A DIRECTORY PREFIX:
There is no directory boundary between company and personal work -- both
are intermixed under Projects/. A prefix rule cannot separate them without
moving ~13 working directories, which would break absolute paths in the
project registry, dev scripts and scheduled tasks. So Fourth repos are
listed. Verbose, but it describes what is actually on disk.
The one prefix that IS meaningful is Projects/fourth/ -- reserved for
future clones from github.com/fourth, which get the right identity
automatically without being added here.
ROUTES are matched LONGEST PREFIX FIRST, compared case-insensitively with
forward slashes, because Windows hands you both spellings.
NOT routed to work, because I could not tell from the repo alone and
guessing an identity is the silent-failure mode this whole design exists
to avoid. They currently fall through to the personal catch-all, which is
their status quo -- so leaving them here changes nothing. Move them into
routes if they are Fourth work.
